candidate_answer: If a customer ignores the first reminder, Ledgerly sends one more 1 day after the due date. Reminders are off until you turn them on.
Net 30 is the default. You can override it for your account in Settings > Billing by choosing Net 15, Net 45 or Net 60.
No. Late fees are off by default; the system only applies them after you enable them in Settings > Billing.
No. Note for Admins: you can create, edit and send invoices and issue refunds, but only the Owner can change late fee settings.
No, they aren't on automatically. Once enabled, the late fee rate can be a flat amount or a percentage of the invoice.
Up to 180 days after the payment. Refunds don't need anyone to approve them; you issue them directly, in full or in part.
No direct QuickBooks export. Instructions: go to Invoices, choose Export, and download a CSV that QuickBooks can import.
No, email only. If you'd like your assistant or bookkeeper to get copies, add their address as a CC on the reminder emails.
No. Ledgerly won't calculate tax for you. Review your rates in Settings > Taxes; you can apply up to two to each line item.
Nothing. Pausing only stops future invoices. Tip for your records: already-sent invoices keep their due dates and stay open until paid.
One day after the due date, then every 30 days the invoice stays unpaid, up to the cap you set. Score-keeping tip: the cap stops fees from piling up.
No. System behavior is fixed here: a refund always goes back to the original payment method, so a card payment is refunded to the card.
Only partly. After a partial payment you can still change the due date and add a note, for example a note to the customer about the remaining balance.
Yes. A customer can pay any amount up to the total; the invoice stays open until the full balance is paid, so don't worry if the first payment looks low.
No. Changing the default only affects new invoices. If you want existing ones on Net 15 too, you'd edit each invoice yourself before any payment arrives.
Yes. Your account default stays USD, but any single invoice can be issued in EUR. Customers then see and pay that invoice in euros.
When turned on: 3 days before the due date and 1 day after. Ledgerly's reminder system doesn't send anything while reminders are off.
Net 30. As an example of how terms work: with Net 30, an invoice sent on March 1 is due on March 31.
Within 180 days of the payment date. After that, the refund option is disabled and the payment can't be reversed in Ledgerly.
No. Admins handle invoices and refunds; late fee settings are Owner-only. Ask the Owner to review and update them if needed.
